[h1] Experienced on the Oculus Rift with the Oculus Remote [/h1]

This is an approximately 45 minute either completely cinematic experience if you choose cinematic or with some interactions if you choose interactive. I had already played this with the interactive elements a while back but for whatever reason my progress wasn't saved on Steam. I found the interactions to be more frustrating than fun. On my second playthrough (I played again today), I chose cinematic and I found the experience more pleasant.

The whole thing starts out with the worst part of the experience (at least for me, especially since I had already seen it), you're in a 1960's small room environment with a retro TV 2D screen looking at old footage of JFK's famous speech about putting man on the moon. It's kind of long and drawn out.  Then you actually get to experience the whole mission to the moon. You are on board Apollo 11 as it is preparing to launch for the lunar mission. You experience take off and leaving Earth's orbit into space. Although you have a first person view of being inside Apollo 11, and the inside cabin looks great, you can't really interact with anything in the cabin. So it's really just a seated cinematic experience.

The interactions that are a part of the experience are linear and scripted and, yes, you can fail which requires repeating the section which can be pretty long. If you've never done the interactive portions then you will probably want to choose the interactive portion, but keep your expectations low.

You finally land on the moon and this is probably the best part of the experience. The vistas from the moon are simply amazing. I just wish you could actually walk around the area (the interactive portion lets you move to some points I believe but it's not what I'm talking about as I wanted to explore as much as possible of the moon). After this, you experience how the astronauts re-entered the Earth. 

I enjoyed the experience, but it's mostly an educational one as the entertainment value is limited to those really interested in the subject matter. This isn't Apollo 11 the movie with all the drama that movies have. Think space documentary with some wow factor from the visuals in VR and that's mostly what you're getting. 

[b]Rate 7/10. The HD version is out now and I personally won't be spending the extra $5 as I don't see how that would significantly improve the experience. It is what it is. It would need a complete overhaul of the script and the interactive elements to be a better game. The visuals really weren't what was lacking in this version.[/b]

This is simply a 'must-have'.

Is it perfect? No.
It is CGI, so you never really lose the feeling of being in a 'game'.

Is it educational? Yes.
I had never actually seen Kennedy's full speech before. At least not that I can remember, but then again; I don't remember most of what he said even after having seen it now :) (Politicians talking... in one ear, out the other)

I played the non-active version, which is basically like watching a movie (I wouldn't mind if more movies where like this! It's definitely more all-engulfing than normal 2D movies (Even 2D 360 movies) :) )

The space-scenes were good, the lunar-surface scenes were better, but no scenes were mind-blowing.

I probably expected more, but I'm not sure I'm making a fair judgement because I had just tried "theBlu", which 'blu' (pun intended, 'blew') me away :) , before this title.

It does give a good perspective on the moon-flight though. And with VR you obviously get a great sense of scale, which is never, or only rarely, really felt in any 2D movies. Especially the moment where Neil is about to set foot on the lunar surface; the LM size really shows.

I would probably have done a few things differently, had I made this title, but I do like it overall.
It IS a very good Apollo11-documentary at this point, but it does leave plenty of room for other takes on this event though (Perhaps also because the Apollo-11 mission is such a huge thing in human history)
